analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. docs/architecture/inference.md changes one table row at line 1163 (gpt_oss). It now states that a bf16 checkpoint keeps bf16 activations and native K/V on every layer, because the expert SwiGLU clamps with scalar bounds that take the activation dtype (GPTOSS+Experts.swift, `swiglu`). docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md line 689 changes the gpt-oss-20b SSD checkpoint size row from float32 K/V on 23 of 24 layers to bf16 K/V on all 24 layers: 24,576 B/token, 154.1 MB at 6,144 tokens, down from 308.0 MB. No source, protocol, key-handling, coordinator-contract or cache-policy code is touched in the supplied evidence.

Relevance to T-041 (SSD prefix cache):
- Cache sizes shrink, so disk-budget and write-endurance exposure is, if anything, lower.
- The documented crypto (DBK3 AES-GCM, HMAC lookup tags, 30-minute TTL, salt scoping) is unchanged.
- The sampler/KV dtype description does not alter identity, AAD or lookup-tag derivation.

Open question, not a finding: the doc asserts a dtype behavior in the code (all-bf16 K/V for gpt-oss). This runtime change is not in the supplied patch. If the code differs, the cache size figures and the observed-dtype gates described in inference.md could be inaccurate. This is a documentation-accuracy matter, not a security regression. The threat model's cache-identity and layout-epoch bindings are not shown to be affected. The unit f9236a49870eace9:0 had only metadata and no content, so there was nothing further to examine. No new attack surface, invalidated assumptions or threat-model gaps identified.
